questions.stem:
PASSAGE A
Asha coordinated a river survey that allowed residents to borrow specialized materials. At first, Asha assumed that adding more items would increase use. A short survey, however, showed that many visitors were uncertain about how to begin. The survey became a compass: it pointed the team toward clearer labels and a one-page guide. During the next month, completed loans rose from 20 to 31. Asha concluded that the collection had not needed to become larger; it had needed to become easier to navigate.

PASSAGE B
A second coordinator, Eli, agreed that instructions matter but argued that conversation is equally important. At Eli's site, volunteers greet new visitors and demonstrate one tool before explaining the catalog. Eli views the catalog as a reference, not a substitute for human guidance.
